prompt: We need to plan a container shipping route from Shanghai to Rotterdam for our new Post-Panamax vessel (beam 48m, draft 20m, capacity 12,000 TEU). The preferred routing is via the Suez Canal to minimize transit time. Based on our scheduling model, the vessel should complete the Shanghai-to-Rotterdam leg in approximately 14 days, allowing us to offer a competitive bi-weekly service. Please design the port rotation, identify any draft or beam restrictions along the route, and confirm the transit time assumptions for our customer-facing schedule.

seeded_faults.description: The vessel has a 20m draft but the Suez Canal maximum permitted draft is approximately 16m (66ft) fully laden. A vessel with 20m draft cannot transit the Suez Canal and would need to route via the Cape of Good Hope.
seeded_faults.location_hint: Vessel draft vs Suez Canal draft limit

seeded_faults.description: A 14-day transit time from Shanghai to Rotterdam via Suez is unrealistic. The actual transit time is 25-30 days at typical service speeds of 14-18 knots, covering approximately 10,000 nautical miles including canal transit and potential port calls.

ground_truth_notes: Suez Canal Authority publishes maximum draft of 66ft (20.1m) for loaded vessels in the new canal, but the original canal is limited to ~16m. Most routing references cite 16m as the practical constraint. Shanghai to Rotterdam via Suez is approximately 10,000 NM; at 16 knots average speed, steaming time alone is ~26 days before adding canal transit time and any port calls. The Cape of Good Hope alternative adds ~3,500 NM and 7-10 days but has no draft restriction.
